title: Galois composita and injective restriction of automorphisms
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be a field extension and let $K,F$ be subfields of $E$ containing $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $K/k$ is finite Galois: finite-dimensional, normal and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Assume $K\vee F=E$, where $K\vee F$ is the smallest subfield of $E$ containing both $K$ and $F$. Then $E/F$ is Galois (normal and separable algebraic). Every $F$-algebra automorphism of $E$ preserves $K$, and restriction is an injective group homomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_k(K)$. A field extension is normal here when the minimal polynomial of every element splits into linear factors over the larger field; a group of field automorphisms has composition as its multiplication.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause, with Mathlib F renamed k and Mathlib L renamed F. IsGalois.sup_right (557–569) gives IsGalois F E from K finite Galois over k and K ⊔ F = top. IsGalois is exactly normal and separable algebraic (54–58). IntermediateField.restrictRestrictAlgEquivMapHom (608–613) defines the restriction group homomorphism; its apply formula (619–621) identifies it with restriction on elements. IntermediateField.restrictRestrictAlgEquivMapHom_injective (623–629) gives injectivity with the same compositum hypothesis. K normal over k is already a consequence of its Galois hypothesis. No change of mathematical notion or tensor-product identification is needed in this leaf.

from.place: Proof Step 3, Gabber finiteness input: the formal Cohen presentation used by ILO V 3.2.1, expanded through IV 4.3.5. Exposé IV 4.3.3–4.3.5, p.60: finite constant extension made Galois before normalized base change, together with the reduced-fibre argument 4.2.3–4.2.4 and the generic Galois observation in 4.3.7, p.61. Equivalently one can take a component and its decomposition group. Field-algebra input for the generic Galois assertion in ILO IV 4.3.7: a Galois constant-field compositum, with restriction to the constants.
